forecasts.reason: Theory: on fresh contests the dial turns unfinished samples into finished ones, but those convert at low precision, so the vote over 4 adds only modestly to the ~49 single; the hard328 vote added ~14 of 328 and RL's added 6.5 on this set.

Theory says fresh contests are where the base fails by not stopping, and the 1.5x dial converts those cap hits (sample 0: 50 right, 14 cap hits vs the base's ~55); converted samples have below-base precision, so the mean sits at RL's single 50.5 rather than above it.

Dose multiplies the near-constant stop-hazard logit: top-1 at 1x already gives 51 cap hits (181 right); doubling it should drive cap hits to ~15-25 and convert a few at low precision, so right answers rise slightly to ~184.

Tripling the top-1 hazard shift leaves almost no cap hits; the converted answers have low precision, and at 3x there is some risk of decay like top-8 at 3x (117), so roughly level with 2x but with a wider interval.
If the 8 directions add a roughly additive stop-hazard logit across layers, one third of the layers at 1.5x is about a 0.5x dose, which scored 170 right with 50 cap hits.
Same additive-hazard reading: a third of the layers at 1.5x is about a 0.5x dose (170/50); nothing in the theory makes the middle layers special.
Same additive-hazard reading as the other layer thirds (about a 0.5x dose, 170/50); late layers hold the readable deliberation directions but get no extra weight under the theory.
Theory treats the edit's effect as a fixed shift in the stop hazard at T 1.0, so new samples land where the stored sample did (427, plain) and only sampling noise is added.

A higher stop hazard means some samples stop early; the edited model opens like the cued base (median right answer ~1,400 tokens, most answers under 2,000), and lengthening of short answers keeps the share under 1,000 tokens at about 22% of 2,000.
Twice the RL change multiplies the stop-hazard shift, so Think-SFT's few MATH-500 cap hits (about 25 of 500) convert at low precision; that adds little to its 457-462 single, near the a=1 467.
Survival view: M(2) scores ~234 at 16,384 tokens with ~54 cap hits; doubling the cap lets most of those finish, and at the ~25% precision of Think-SFT's late finishes that adds about 8-10.
At 2x the dial leaves almost no cap hits, but precision falls (0.59 vs 0.65 on hard328, 190 vs 203); on MATH-500, which has few cap hits, that means a small drop from the 1.5x cell's 456.

The base fails on fresh contests by not stopping; without the cue the plain base stops early on short, low-precision answers, which gives about 0.46 of the cued single 29.5, the same ratio as hard328 (76 vs 164).
